question: What must a Speed Limit sign display, in what increments, and may it be used to show an advisory speed for a roadway condition?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A Speed Limit (R2-1) sign must display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study, and the displayed speed limits must be in multiples of 5 mph. A Speed Limit sign should not be used to show an advisory speed for a roadway condition; instead, an Advisory Speed plaque mounted below a warning sign is the recommended (and permitted) device for that purpose. Standards (mandatory): - "The Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Figure 2B-3) shall display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study. The speed limits displayed shall be in multiples of 5 mph." - For variable speed limit signs: "The regulatory speed displayed on a variable Speed Limit sign shall comply with Paragraph 13 of" Section 2B.21 (i.e., the same display requirements apply). Guidance (recommended): - As shown in the page text visible in [Image 3]: "An advisory speed plaque (see Section 2C.59) mounted below a warning sign should be used to warn road users of an advisory speed for a roadway condition. A Speed Limit sign should not be used for this purpose." Options (permitted): - "An Advisory Speed plaque (see Figure 2C-1 and Section 2C.59) may be used when the change in roadway condition requires a reduced speed." - "An Advisory Exit Speed or Advisory Ramp Speed sign may be used based on engineering judgment when the difference between the mainline roadway speed limit and the exit or ramp advisory speed in the vicinity of the departure is 10 mph or less." - "A Speed Limit Sign Beacon may be used with a fixed or variable Speed Limit sign," and a flashing beacon with an appropriate accompanying sign may indicate that the displayed speed limit is in effect. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-3 shows the Speed Limit (R2-1) sign displaying "SPEED LIMIT 50" along with related speed limit signs and plaques (e.g., R2-2P TRUCKS, R2-4P MINIMUM, R2-4a SPEED LIMIT/MINIMUM), all with limits in multiples of 5 mph. - [Image 2] Shows curve warning sign layouts where advisory speeds (35 MPH) are conveyed by W13-1P Advisory Speed plaques mounted below warning signs (W1-2, W1-8), not by Speed Limit signs. - [Image 3] Shows the text of Section 2B.21, including Standard Paragraph 13 (display of the established limit in multiples of 5 mph) and the Guidance that a Speed Limit sign should not be used to warn of an advisory speed for a roadway condition. - [Image 4] Shows Figure 2B-3 (Speed Limit Signs and Plaques) with the R2-1 sign and related plaques, all displaying speeds in multiples of 5 mph. - [Image 5] Shows examples of enhanced conspicuity for signs, including a SPEED LIMIT 35 sign with flags, illustrating regulatory (not advisory) use of the R2-1 sign. Citations: - Section 2B.21 Standard §13 (p.85) - Section 2G.26 Standard §3 (p.457) - Section 2C.28 Option §2 (p.173) - Section 2C.12 Option §5 (p.160) - Section 4S.04 Option §3 (p.753) - Figure 2B-3 (p.86) - Page 126
gold_answer: It must display the speed limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or an authorized agency based on an engineering study, in multiples of 5 mph. It should not be used for an advisory speed; an advisory speed plaque below an appropriate warning sign should be used instead.
